newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt government paper sees no hope from Netanyahu.
newsitem.headline: Egypt government paper sees no hope from Netanyahu.

text.p: An Egyptian government newspaper said on Monday a change of government in Israel was probably needed for the sake of progress towards Middle East peace.

A front-page editorial in al-Akhbar said the present government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was trying to undermine old agreements with the Palestinians, and hardliners in his government would pounce on him anyway if he looked likely to make progress in talks with the Palestinians.

"Netanyahu is still fumbling around, sticking to the policy of beating about the bush in an attempt to abort the peace agreements, firstly as a political aim of his aggressive strategy and secondly to save his government from collapse."
Netanyahu was elected prime minister for a four-year term in May.
"In Washington everyone knows there is no hope of movement under the shadow of the Netanyahu government's hostility to peace," the newspaper said.

"This government in its present form is absolutely incapable of taking a positive decision which would help pacify the fury of the Palestinians...who are waiting to see what will come out of Israel's delays and procrastinations," it added.

"Nobody expects to believe Netanyahu when he claims every day there are signs of a solution to the crisis over negotiations with the Palestinians, while the hardline crows in his government...wait in ambush for any move in that direction.

"The Israeli government is in reality fragmented and at risk of collapse at any moment because of discord and conflicts of interest. (All this) calls for pessimism that Netanyahu is capable of taking a decision in favour of the peace process, contrary to what he is trying to make Israeli and international public opinion believe," it added.
The editorial, by chief editor Galal Duweidar, said Israelis were describing Netanyahu as inexperienced and politically unaware but it did not add any personal attacks of its own.
After Israeli criticism of the Egyptian press last week, President Hosni Mubarak said on Saturday he would like the Egyptian media to avoid what he called "base expressions".
